title: Cepillo Green avocado (Cepillo avocado): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Cepillo Green avocado: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Cepillo Green avocado is an avocado variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Cepillo Green is a registered avocado variety, also sold or known as Cepillo avocado or NSIC Av 01. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1995 as NSIC 1995 Av 01. Gualberto Cepillo bred it. Its record notes a yield of 300 to 350 fruits.

blocks.text: Key facts about Cepillo Green avocado
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Cepillo Green was about 52 years old when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 300 to 350 fruits. It bears every year, with fruit in May July. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit avocado fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Cepillo Green weighs about 719.4 grams, and its shape is pyriform. The flesh is dark yellow and smooth and fine. The edible part is 79.4 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is May July, bearing annual.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Pear shaped, about 720 g, green, leathery skin, dark yellow, smooth, fiberless flesh, buttery and nutty, about 79 percent edible.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: big, green skinned Batangas avocado (about 720 g) with buttery, nutty flesh. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Cepillo Green avocado

Grafted avocado bears sooner and true to type. Pick a selection by fruit size and flesh, and plant two kinds that flower at different times of day for better fruit set. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Cepillo avocado the same as Cepillo Green?
items.a: Yes. Cepillo avocado is another name for Cepillo Green, registered as NSIC 1995 Av 01. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 300 to 350 fruits. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Cepillo Green?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
